In [[algebraic geometry]],  '''Du Bois singularities''' are singularities of [[complex algebraic variety|complex varieties]] studied by Du Bois.<ref>{{harvtxt|Du Bois|1981}}</ref> 

Schwede<ref>{{harvtxt|Schwede|2007|p=1|loc=Thm 4.6}}</ref> gave the following characterisation of Du Bois singularities. Suppose that <math>X</math> is a [[reduced scheme|reduced]] [[closed subscheme]] of a [[smooth scheme]] <math>Y</math>.

Take a log resolution <math>\pi: Z \to Y</math> of <math>X</math> in <math>Y</math> that is an isomorphism outside <math>X</math>, and let <math>E</math> be the reduced preimage of <math>X</math> in <math>Z</math>. Then <math>X</math> has Du Bois singularities if and only if the induced map <math>\mathcal{O}_X \to R\pi_{*}\mathcal{O}_E</math> is a [[quasi-isomorphism]].
